submit_summary: The binary at /input/target is a stripped Go HTTP server application built with CGO support. It is likely obfuscated (using garble based on mangled type names visible in strings like "main.fItsZo", "main.e_2OTc"). The server listens on address 127.0.0.1:8080 by default (configurable via "-addr" flag) and implements a note-taking API with four HTTP endpoints: /v1/register (for user registration), /v1/note/put (to store notes), /v1/note/get (to retrieve notes), and /v1/note/list (to list all notes). The binary uses net/http for the HTTP server infrastructure and includes extensive Go runtime, crypto, and TLS support. I've created a basic Go module structure with stub implementations of the main server and handlers in /work/main.go, which compiles successfully. However, the actual implementation details of each endpoint (request/response formats, data persistence, authentication logic) remain unrecovered due to the obfuscation and time constraints. Full reverse engineering would require binary diff analysis against an unobfuscated version, detailed disassembly analysis of the handler functions, or dynamic runtime tracing.
